newsitem.title: FRANCE: France cites signs of foreign presence in Zaire.
newsitem.headline: France cites signs of foreign presence in Zaire.

text.p: France said on Friday there were growing signs that fighters from Zaire's eastern neigbours had entered Zaire, but could not confirm that regular army units were involved.
Foreign Ministry spokesman Jacques Rummelhardt said Paris was worried by indications that "elements" from countries bordering eastern Zaire were fighting alongside rebels.
"We do not have at this stage confirmation that units from the regular armed forces of Zaire'e eastern neighbours are involved in the fighting," he told a news briefing.
Rummelhardt declined to be more precise and give details of what indications he based his statement on.
The Foreign Ministry in Belgium, Zaire's former colonial master, said earlier this week there were growing but still unconfirmed indications that thousands of Rwandan soldiers were in Zaire.
Zaire accuses Rwanda, Burundi and most recently Uganda of invading to back the rebels, who launched their offensive in October and hold towns and territory in the east.
All three deny their troops are fighting inside Zaire.
Zaire has ruled out negotiations with the rebels and launched a counter-offensive. It has acknowledged its mercenary-backed army had run into resistance on several fronts.
France has repeatedly voiced support for Zaire's territorial integrity, and for President Mobutu Sese Seko, who it says is the man best placed to prevent a break-up of the country.
Zairean deputy prime minister in charge of foreign affairs, Kamanda wa Kamanda, is due to visit Paris on Monday on his way home from New York.
France has tense relations with the Tutsi-led Rwandan government which accused Paris of backing the former Hutu government responsible for 1994 massacres of half a million Tutsis and moderate Hutus.

France set a safe area in Rwanda and eastern Zaire as more than a million Hutus fled retaliation after the Tutsis took over, drawing charges from Kigali that it was sheltering those guilty of genocide.

Paris was among the main proponents late last year of a multinational force to help Rwandan, mainly Hutu, refugees caught in eastern Zaire in the fighting between Zairean forces and rebels backed by the Tutsi-led Rwandan government.
The force was approved by the United Nations and later shelved after most of the refugees returned home.
